nodes.t: The Lani are an indigenous people in Puncak, Central Papua and Lanny Jaya, Highland Papua, usually labelled 'Western Dani' by foreign missionaries, or grouped—inaccurately—with the Dani people who inhabit the Baliem Valley to the east.

First contact with the populous Lani was made in October 1920 during the Central New Guinea Expedition, in which a group of explorers stayed for six months with them at their farms in the upper Swart River Valley (now Toli Valley, Tolikara Regency).
The total population of Lani tribes in the 1980s, as reported by Douglas Hayward in his book The Dani of Irian Jaya, Before and After Conversion was around 200,000 people.
The most distinguishable feature of the Lani and Dani tribes is their kotekas, or penis gourds made from the bottle gourd.
Meanwhile Lani women wear two types of skirt made of barks, the colourful green, yellow, red, and purple sali koe or the brown and purple tipped skirt called sali keragi.

nodes.t: Yali are a major tribal group in Highland Papua in Indonesia, and live to the east of the Baliem Valley, mainly in Yalimo Regency, Yahukimo Regency, and the surrounding regions.

In general, the Yali are split into two groups, Yali (mo) and Yali Mek, which live in Yalimo Regency and Yahukimo Regency, respectively. They also speak two different languages, the first one related to the Dani in the Ngalik-Nduga subfamily, the other one related to the Mek.
The settlement territory of the Yali lies between the rivers Ubahak to the east and Sibi, Yahuli, and Podeng to the west.

Accounts of the population size vary according to the source. In 1991, it was estimated to be 15,000 or 30,000. While according to the 2010 Indonesian census, the population was 133,812; however, this figure included Ngalik people.
The Yali use sweet potatoes and taro as their staple foods, which are grown using shifting cultivation. Other food sources are hunting and gathering.

nodes.t: Suku Yali adalah kelompok etnis yang mendiami Provinsi Papua Pegunungan, Indonesia.
Suku Yali membentuk kampung-kampung kecil yang tersebar di daerah pegunungan tengah, di sebelah timur dari lembah Baliem.
Orang Yali juga terbagi-bagi menurut bahasa, dialek, dan budayanya, menjadi dua kelompok besar: Yalimek dan Yalimo.
Perbedaan ini mencakup juga bahasa karena suku Yali memiliki dua bahasa, bahasa Yali (rumpun bahasa Lembah Baliem), sedangkan kelompok lain berbahasa Mek.

nodes.t: Under the Mountain Wall: A Chronicle of Two Seasons in the Stone Age
nodes.x: Narrative account of the 1961 Harvard-Peabody Expedition among the southern Kurelu in the Baliem Valley, from the author's introduction. It says the Baliem was spotted from the air in 1938, no outsider lived there until a government post in 1954, and describes the alliance structure of Kurelu and members of the expedition (Gardner, Heider, Broekhuijse, Rockefeller). Journalistic rather than academic; describes warfare and ritual.

nodes.t: Expedition Content and the Harvard Peabody Expedition to Netherlands New Guinea, 1961
nodes.x: Article on the film Dead Birds and the 1961 expedition. The snippet notes the expedition organiser's use of the name 'Dani' and that the group now prefers another name.

nodes.t: Archbold Expedition to New Guinea (3rd: 1938-1939), AMNH archives agent record
nodes.x: Archive record with a dated chronology of the 1938-39 expedition sponsored by AMNH, the Zoologisch Museum, the Dutch military and Richard Archbold, with camps at Lake Habbema and Bernhard Camp, and Baliem Valley contact with local people in late 1938. It also notes ethnological notes on tribes.

nodes.t: A Generous Facilitator (Archbold and the Baliem)
nodes.x: Biographical article on Richard Archbold. The retrieved opening says the Grand Valley of the Baliem and its large Dani population was seen from the air on 23 June 1938 by the Guba flying boat crew, and that a Baliem camp in December 1938 collected specimens and early observations of inhabitants.

nodes.t: Dead Birds: The 'Theater' of War among the Dugum Dani
nodes.x: Abstract: argues that battles among the Dugum Dani, often read via the film Dead Birds as ritualised combat, involved real attempts to kill that were blunted by waterlogged terrain, with fighting confined to raised strips. Concerns Dani warfare history, not sacred rites.

nodes.t: Tim Kemanusiaan Nduga rampung verifikasi korban kemanusiaan (ANTARA)
nodes.x: ANTARA reports the Nduga Humanitarian Team, which says it was formed by the regency government, verified at least 184 deaths in Nduga between December 2018 and July 2019, most from illness, hunger and cold while displaced; Theo Hesegem says three actors are involved: civilians, TNI/Polri and the OPM. Breakdown given by age and sex.

nodes.t: Temuan soal dampak operasi pengejaran KKB di Nduga; Masyarakat Nduga trauma, ribuan mengungsi
nodes.x: Kompas reports an independent investigation team (church figures, MRP members, Theo Hesegem) presented preliminary findings on 29 March 2019 at Amnesty Indonesia's office, with per-district displacement counts such as 4,276 in Mapenduma and 5,056 in Jigi, and the missing Pastor Geyimin Nirigi. It reports an emergency school with 697 pupils in Wamena. Armed-group attack in December 2018 on Istaka Karya workers triggered the operation.

nodes.t: Human Rights Investigators: Bombs dropped, hospitals torched and thousands displaced in Nduga
nodes.x: ULMWP, a pro-independence organisation, reports the investigation team estimated over 32,000 internally displaced, 34 schools damaged and allegations of helicopter bombing; these are the team's claims and the Indonesian government has said otherwise (see US State Dept: 3,000 displaced per Ministry of Social Affairs).
nodes.a: ULMWP (reporting the Nduga Case Investigation Team)

nodes.t: OHCHR special procedures communication on forced displacement in Nduga
nodes.x: UN experts' communication to Indonesia reports information that security operations began on 4 December 2018 after TPN-PB reportedly killed at least 17 contractors; that at least nine Papuans were killed and five missing; that at least thirteen displaced persons died of exhaustion, hunger and hypothermia; and that about 2,000 people had sought refuge in Jayawijaya by March 2019. It records these as allegations put to the government.

nodes.t: Human Rights and Conflict Escalation in West Papua (ICP, with 2019 update)
nodes.x: ICP reports that human rights defenders counted 189 civilian fatalities from Nduga between December 2018 and 10 October 2019, including at least 41 children, and that no camp was set up so exact displacement is unknown. Compare 184 (Nduga Humanitarian Team, to July 2019), 'officials estimated 53' (US State Dept), and 3,000 to 20,000 displaced (government versus media).

nodes.t: Indonesia: Investigate Riot Deaths in Papua (Wamena)
nodes.x: HRW reports at least 33 deaths in Wamena riots from 23 September 2019, and that police listed 8 Papuans and 25 people from elsewhere in Indonesia among the dead. It reports at least 8,000 displaced since 29 September and an internet shutdown from 23 to 29 September, and urges a Komnas HAM investigation.

nodes.t: Wamena 2019: Komnas HAM statements (Anadolu Agency, ANTARA, detik)
nodes.x: Komnas HAM chair reported 31 deaths and thousands displaced on 30 September 2019 (5,000 at Wamena police, 2,700 at the district military command), then 33 per hospital data and a further 10 unconfirmed deaths buried in home villages. He said an alleged racist remark by a teacher was not confirmed, and that victims included both migrants and local Papuans. The Jayawijaya government recorded 7,278 people in shelters at over 59 points.

nodes.t: Peace cannot be achieved in Papua if human rights are not respected (Amnesty International Indonesia)
nodes.x: Amnesty Indonesia reports that from January to June 2021 at least 6,152 people were forced to leave their homes in Papua and West Papua, and refers to the killing of a nurse in Kiwirok.

nodes.t: 'Destroy them first... discuss human rights later': Investigation of Indonesian Security Forces' operations in Papua's Kiwirok
nodes.x: HRM reports that between 13 September and late October 2021 security forces attacked eight villages in Kiwirok, with 206 buildings destroyed per satellite imagery, at least 2,252 Ngalum displaced as of June 2023 and at least 72 IDPs reported dead by 23 July 2023; it reports no direct civilian deaths in the raids. It says armed resisters burned schools and public buildings used as bases and calls for a Komnas HAM inquiry.

nodes.t: Displaced and disempowered (Kiwirok, Pegunungan Bintang)
nodes.x: TAPOL reports operations began after a September 2021 attack on a Kiwirok clinic in which two clinic staff were killed, that security forces blamed TPNPB while some local sources attributed it to local political feuds, and that the cause of displacement is disputed: the military says villagers fled armed groups, while people TAPOL spoke to say they fled operations. Three deaths on the journey to Oksibil are reported.

nodes.t: Nakes di Papua minta jaminan keamanan setelah serangan Puskesmas oleh KKB (BBC Indonesia) and ANTARA Papua coverage
nodes.x: BBC Indonesia reports a health worker died in the 13 September 2021 attack on Kiwirok health centre, said to be the first reported attack on a health facility in Papua, that nine of 11 staff were evacuated and health workers elsewhere were withdrawn to Oksibil. ANTARA reports Komnas HAM Papua protecting the health workers and clinic closures.
